input: Reseal the driveway before the rainy season

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The driveway material (asphalt, concrete, pavers) determines which products and techniques are needed — the entire process differs by surface type.
Knowing exactly when the rainy season starts sets a hard deadline that shapes how urgently prep and application must be scheduled.
The current condition of the driveway — cracks, stains, previous sealant — determines how much prep work (cleaning, crack-filling) is needed before sealing.
Whether the user plans to DIY or hire a contractor completely changes the plan — tools, costs, and steps involved differ significantly.
The size of the driveway affects how much sealant to buy, how long the job takes, and whether equipment like a squeegee applicator or sprayer is needed.
Some sealants prioritize durability, others UV resistance or a specific finish (matte vs. glossy) — the user's priority shapes which product to recommend.
Understanding what the user considers a successful result — protection only, improved appearance, or both — determines the standard the plan should aim for.

gold.taskTitle: Reseal driveway before rainy season starts
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to reseal their driveway in time for the rainy season, which involves preparing the surface and applying a sealant.

questions.title: What material is your driveway made of?
questions.description: Is the driveway asphalt, concrete, pavers, or another material? This determines which sealant products and application methods apply.

questions.title: When exactly does your rainy season begin?
questions.description: Knowing the target date sets a hard deadline for scheduling prep, application, and the required curing time before rain arrives.

questions.title: What condition is the driveway surface in right now?
questions.description: Are there visible cracks, oil stains, peeling old sealant, or is it relatively clean and intact? This drives how much prep work is needed.

questions.title: Are you planning to do this yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: A DIY approach requires sourcing tools and products; hiring a contractor shifts the plan toward getting quotes and vetting professionals.

questions.title: How large is the driveway approximately in square feet?
questions.description: The surface area determines how much sealant to purchase and whether specialized application equipment is worth renting.

questions.title: Do you prioritize durability, appearance, or both equally?
questions.description: Some sealants are formulated for maximum protection, others for a clean finish — knowing the priority guides the product selection.

questions.title: What does a great result look like to you when done?
questions.description: Is the goal purely weatherproofing, restoring the look of the driveway, or a combination? This defines the standard the plan should meet.
